questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Deprecations pose production risk in multi-tenant clusters. This question probes practical policy design across CI and runtime using Gatekeeper and Kyverno, plus concrete manifests and validation strategy.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno admission policies
- Kubernetes API deprecations and upgrade paths
- CI validation with kubeconform/kubeval
- Runtime admission controls and auditability

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sdeprecatedapi
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sDeprecatedAPI
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sdeprecatedapi
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        deprecated := ["apps/v1beta1", "networking.k8s.io/v1beta1"]
        api := input.review.object.apiVersion
        api == deprecated[_]
        msg := sprintf("deprecated apiVersion used: %v", [api])
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (deprecated API)
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: old-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/old:1
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (stable API)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: new-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/new:1
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to cover CRDs and future API regressions?
- How would you surface violations to developers and enforce remediation in PRs?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests end-to-end image provenance across multi-cloud GPU workloads, combining CI, runtime policies, and verification in real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance, Cosign, Sigstore, reproducible builds
- Kubernetes admission control (Kyverno/OPA)
- Buildx/OCI digests and registry security
- GPU workload constraints and cross-cloud policy

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: build, sign, verify
name: BuildSignVerify
on: [push]
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up QEMU/Buildx
      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          docker buildx create --use
          image=registry.example.com/project/image:${{ github.sha }}
          docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
            -t $image --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1 .
          cosign sign -key cosign.key $image
          docker push $image
      - name: Verify signature
        run: cosign verify -key cosign.pub $image
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-image
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: check-cosign-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    verifyImages:
    - image: registry.example.com/*
      pattern: "^.+$"
```

```yaml
# Sample failing manifest (unsigned image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: guest-deploy
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/project/image:unsigned

```

```yaml
# Sample passing manifest (signed image with digest)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-deploy
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        build.sha256: "abcdef123456..."
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/project/image:sha-abcdef
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test policy changes across multiple clusters with blue/green deployments?
- What are failure modes if cosign keys rotate or GitOps sync lags?

## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates practical supply chain security controls in multi-cloud Kubernetes environments. It assesses familiarity with policy-as-code, container image signature verification, and SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) attestations integrated into CI/CD pipelines.

## Key Concepts

- **Image Provenance:** Cosign and Sigstore provide cryptographic verification that container images have not been tampered with and originate from trusted sources.
- **SBOM Attestations:** Software Bill of Materials documents enumerate software components, enabling vulnerability tracking and compliance verification.
- **Policy-as-Code:** Gatekeeper and Kyverno enforce admission control policies as code, ensuring consistent security enforcement across clusters.
- **Multi-Cloud Complexity:** Different cloud providers require unified security controls; policy engines provide a vendor-agnostic approach to image verification.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical enforcement of runtime posture using admission controls and network egress in a multi-tenant data platform. Combines Gatekeeper and Kyverno with real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate with REGO to require envoy-proxy sidecar in confidential pods
- Kyverno policy enforcing non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem and sidecar presence
- NetworkPolicy egress allowlist for data exfiltration guardrails
- CI test plan with manifest validation; runtime validation via in-cluster policy, egress monitoring

## Code Example
```rego
package k8svalidation

deny["envoy-proxy sidecar required"] {
  input.review.object.metadata.labels["data-tier"] == "confidential"
  not has_sidecar(input.review.object.spec.containers, "envoy-proxy")
}

has_sidecar(containers, name) {
  containers[i].name == name
}
```

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: confidential-pod-security
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-envoy-sidecar
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              data-tier: confidential
    validate:
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: envoy-proxy
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

# ConstraintTemplate (ImageProvenanceAndSecurity)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: imageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package imageprovenance
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          some i

          startswith(image, "registry.example.com/")
          not endswith(image, ":latest")

          msg := "image must be from registry.example.com with digest"
        }

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to encode security baselines as policy-as-code and enforce them in CI/CD pipelines for multi-tenant clusters. It tests understanding of threat modeling, policy granularity, and how to allow exceptions in a controlled manner.

## Key Concepts

- **Open Policy Agent (OPA) with Rego**: Declarative policy language for Kubernetes admission control
- **Pod Security Standards**: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privilege escalation, and security profiles
- **Volume Security**: hostPath, hostNetwork, and hostPID considerations in multi-tenant environments

## Rego Policy

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
  msg := "Containers must run as non-root (runAsNonRoot: true)"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.privileged == true
  msg := "Privileged containers are not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
  msg := "Containers must use readOnlyRootFilesystem"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.object.spec.hostNetwork == true
  msg := "hostNetwork is not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.object.spec.hostPID == true
  msg := "hostPID is not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  volume := input.request.object.spec.volumes[_]
  volume.hostPath
  not allowed_hostpath[volume.hostPath.path]
  msg := sprintf("hostPath volume %s is not allowed", [volume.hostPath.path])
}

allowed_hostpath {
  input.request.namespace == "kube-system"
}

allowed_hostpath[path] {
  allowed_paths := [""]
  path := allowed_paths[_]
}
```

## Failing Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: false
      privileged: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
  hostNetwork: true
  hostPID: true
  volumes:
  - name: data
    hostPath:
      path: /var/data
```

## Passing Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
  namespace: production
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:stable
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      privileged: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      seccompProfile:
        type: RuntimeDefault
  securityContext:
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. **Install OPA CLI**: `brew install opa` or download from https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/
2. **Test Rego policy**: `opa eval --format pretty --data policy.rego --input failing-pod.json "data.kubernetes.admission.deny"`
3. **Verify failing manifest**: Should return denial messages for each violated policy
4. **Verify passing manifest**: Should return empty deny array
5. **CI/CD Integration**: Add OPA gate to your pipeline:
   ```yaml
   # GitHub Actions example
   - name: Run OPA Gate
     run: |
       opa eval --format json --data policy.rego --input pod.json "data.kubernetes.admission.deny" > results.json
       if [ $(jq '.result[0].expressions[0].value | length' results.json) -gt 0 ]; then
         echo "Policy violations found:"
         jq '.result[0].expressions[0].value' results.json
         exit 1
       fi
   ```
6. **Deploy to cluster**: Apply the OPA Gatekeeper constraints via Gatekeeper's ConstraintTemplate system.

This question evaluates real-world expertise in supply chain security by testing the ability to tie SBOMs to runtime admission policies. It aligns with vendor-agnostic security frameworks (SLSA, SBOM) and modern GitOps deployment patterns where provenance verification is critical.

## Key Concepts

- **CycloneDX SBOMs**: Standardized software bills of materials that document container contents
- **Image digests**: SHA256 references ensuring immutable image pinning
- **Kyverno admission control**: Policy engine validating deployments at Kubernetes admission time
- **Helm chart provenance**: Ensuring charts reference verified, SBOM-backed images

## Proposed Solution

### GitHub Actions Workflow: Generate and Publish SBOMs

```yaml
name: SBOM Pipeline
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-and-sbom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          format: cyclonedx-json
          image: ${{ github.repository }}
          output-file: sbom.json
      - run: |
          echo "${{ steps.sbom.outputs.sbom-json }}" | ghcr.io/your-org/sbom-store:latest 
            --image=${{ github.repository }}@${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
```

### Kyverno Policy: Enforce SBOM Presence at Admission

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-image-sbom
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: validate-sbom-present
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
        - Deployment
        - StatefulSet
        - DaemonSet
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: "{{ request.operation }}"
        operator: In
        value: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    validate:
      message: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        deny:
          conditions:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: ""
          - key: "{{ lookup('sbom.verify', '{{ element.image }}', 'cyclonedx') }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: "valid"
```

### Failing Manifest (No SBOM)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vulnerable-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vulnerable-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vulnerable-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.25
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment blocked with error: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"

### Passing Manifest (SBOM Verified)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: verified-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: verified-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: verified-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: ghcr.io/your-org/app@sha256:a1b2c3d4e5f6...
        annotations:
          sbom.cyclonedx: "ghcr.io/your-org/app/sbom/a1b2c3d4e5f6"
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment allowed

## Testing Steps

1. **Apply Kyverno policy**: `kubectl apply -f kyverno-policy.yaml`
2. **Test failing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-no-sbom.yaml` — should be rejected
3. **Test passing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-with-sbom.yaml` — should be admitted
4. **Verify SBOM storage**: Confirm SBOMs are queryable via your SBOM service endpoint
5. **Audit logs**: Check Kyverno policy reports for enforcement details
